title: GPU memory budgeting and dynamic headroom plan for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement deterministic GPU memory budgets that split capacity across model weights, KV cache growth, and transient activations for continuous-batching workloads. Produce a runtime strategy that: 1) prevents OOM during bursty streaming/continuous batching, 2) minimizes conservative overprovisioning, and 3) provides runtime-adjustable headroom and eviction/ offload policies tied to SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can compute per-backend memory budget (weights, KV, activations) before model warmup and refuse + surface config when insufficient headroom.
Continuous-batcher demonstrates <1% request failure due to OOM across 48h soak with mixed-length traffic when using computed budgets vs current baseline.
KV offload path to host memory enabled with <10ms median penalty for warm hits and fails gracefully to eviction when host memory exhausted.
Documentation and console UI surfaces per-model budget breakdown and a telemetry dashboard (per-route tokens, peak KV size, activations peak).
proposed_solution: Create a per-model memory profile at model-load that estimates: static_weights, reserve_for_optimizers(none in runtime), per_token_kv_bytes, per_token_activation_bytes (for worst-case sequence length and batch), plus configurable headroom percentage. Use these to compute an allocation vector: weights_pinned = ceil(weights_bytes aligned), kv_budget = max(min_kv, traffic_estimated * per_token_kv_bytes + margin), activation_budget = peak_batch * per_token_activation_bytes + margin. Implement a slab allocator with three pools to bound fragmentation and enable fast failure path. Add two dynamic mitigations: (A) KV compression/quantization (FP16/INT8/4-bit) toggles per-model, and (B) offload-to-host with async prefetch/eviction for large KV populations. Expose autoscaler hooks so Dedicated autoscaler can buy extra GPUs when headroom deficit persists beyond a threshold.
decisions: Adopt three-pool slab allocator (weights/kv/activations) rather than single shared pool to simplify enforcement and telemetry.
Default headroom margin = 12% (configurable per-customer); will iterate to 8–20% based on model family and observed fragmentation.
Enable optional KV host-offload for models with per-token KV > 256 bytes; offload disabled by default for latency-sensitive tiers.
Prefer compression (FP16) over host-offload when compute budget allows, to preserve latency.
Expose package-level flags (runtime config) and console toggles for aggressive eviction vs. conservative offload policies.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes. Collected initial telemetry (runtime-telemetry-2026-02-20) showing KV growth dominates peak GPU usage for conversational routes with >2048 context. Proposed building estimators per-model and validating against 7-day traces.

2026-03-02 - Luca Moretti: Initial prototype of allocator in branch github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/432. Prototype enforces pool caps and returns a clear error when activations exceed budget. Need to wire per-model profile generator.

2026-03-04 - PM review (Jordan Lee): Requested customer-facing behavior: when headroom insufficient, surface recommended actions in Console (reduce max_context, enable kv-compression, or request Dedicated burst). Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-06 - Design feedback (Maya Chen): Suggested small Console UX: show three stacked bars for weights/KV/activations and a tooltip explaining offload/compression trade-offs. File: drive.google.com/designs/runtime-memory-ui-v1

2026-03-08 - Engineering update (Luca Moretti): Benchmarks on rtx-a100-80gb: sample model (Redwood-13B) weights=26GB (quantized FP16=13GB), steady-state KV per-conversation=128KB, expansion at 50 concurrent convs = ~6.4GB KV. Activations peak with batch=8 at 4GB. With 12% headroom, available for burst = 9.6GB. Without compression host-offload triggered frequently. Next: add BK-tree compression experiment and measure latency tail.

2026-03-10 - Security note (Hannah Torres): KMS/HSM not impacted; KV never leaves ephemeral instance storage unless offloaded to host memory within runtime tenant. Need to add audit log when KV is offloaded.
notes: This ticket coordinates runtime allocator changes, telemetry dashboards, console UX, and Dedicated autoscaler integration. Cross-team sync needed with Console (PM/design) and Ops for Dedicated capacity planning.
